Synopsis: The player sided with the drow and goblins and participated in the massacre of the grove. Gale is shocked by what happened and the fact that he participated in the slaughter. He wants to leave, so the player has to convince him to stay if indeed he wants Gale to stay. The mood and tone are dour and dark. retrieved_synopses: You and your party sided with the drow and goblins and took part in the grove’s slaughter; the excerpts show the bloody aftermath and Gale’s horror at having participated. Gale is wracked with guilt, lashes out accusatorily at the player, and says he wants to leave — the player must decide whether to calm, cajole, or confront him to keep him in the party. The tone is dour and accusatory, with Gale framing his anguish as both personal corruption and something the player led him into. Off-screen relationships (for example prior dealings with Mol and her Den gang) have already shaped how others view the party, but the immediate scene centers on Gale’s shock and the player’s attempt to hold him.

Takes place immediately after the player blows the horn at the gates of the grove, beginning an attack on the refugees hiding there. The surviving tiefling leader rallies his troops, then the drow commander arrives with her retinue of goblins. She mind-melds with the player. She expects them - as True Souls - to betray the tieflings, and players must choose whether to side with her OR with the tieflings as the attack begins.

This is a huge fight and a decisive moment for the tieflings, the drow/goblins, AND the players.

The player has done too many things that upset Gale or make your reputation with him fall below a certain threshold. When that moment is reached, Gale decides to leave the party. It is a tense moment. To reach this point the player must have done many things that upset him.

If the player sided with the goblins and helped sack the Grove, Halsin (if still alive) will show up at a subsequent camp night seeking vengeance. There's no way to calm him - the dialogue will always end with combat against him and some animals.

One of the goblins is torturing a prisoner, either to find out where the grove is, or just because he wants to. The player can try to get rid of him - if Shadowheart is present, she gives some advice on how to do so. If Shadowheart is the avatar, she has unique options criticising the goblin's techniques.
context: You and your party joined the drow and goblins in sacking the grove — the player blew the horn to begin the attack and the massacre just finished — and Gale is horrified that he helped carry it out. He is consumed by guilt, lashes out at the player as the cause of his corruption, and threatens to leave the party unless you can calm, cajole, or confront him into staying. Off-screen consequences (how others now view the group, possible retaliation such as Halsin’s later vengeance, and prior friction with factions like Mol’s den) have already been set, but the immediate scene focuses on Gale’s anguish and your attempt to hold him. The mood is dour and accusatory; how you respond determines whether Gale remains or departs.
